definitions.explanation: Appearing physically or emotionally weak, delicate, or fragile.

examples.japanese: {弱々|よわよわ}しい{声|こえ}で{答|こた}えた。
examples.english: I answered in a feeble voice.

examples.japanese: {病気|びょうき}の{後|あと}、{彼|かれ}は{弱々|よわよわ}しく{見|み}えた。
examples.english: After his illness, he looked frail.

examples.japanese: {弱々|よわよわ}しい{光|ひかり}が{窓|まど}から{差|さ}し{込|こ}んでいた。
examples.english: A faint light was streaming in through the window.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}の{弱々|よわよわ}しい{足取|あしど}りが{心配|しんぱい}だった。
examples.english: I was worried about my grandmother's frail steps.

notes:
An emphatic form of {弱|よわ}い created by reduplication ({弱|よわ} + {弱|よわ} + しい). Emphasizes the appearance or impression of weakness rather than actual weakness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弱々|よわよわ}しい{声|こえ} — a feeble voice
- {弱々|よわよわ}しい{光|ひかり} — a faint light
- {弱々|よわよわ}しい{足取|あしど}り — frail footsteps
- {弱々|よわよわ}しい{笑|え}み — a weak smile
- {弱々|よわよわ}しく{見|み}える — to look frail

WORD FORMATION:
This follows the common Japanese pattern of reduplicating an adjective stem to create a しい-adjective that emphasizes appearance or impression:
- {弱|よわ}い → {弱々|よわよわ}しい (weak-looking)
- {痛|いた}い → {痛々|いたいた}しい (painful-looking, pitiful)
- {初々|ういうい}しい (fresh, innocent-looking)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {弱|よわ}い — weak (direct, objective)
- {華奢|きゃしゃ} — delicate, slender (can be positive)
- {頼|たよ}りない — unreliable, flimsy
